📖 How to use

  1. Enter the monthly pension, the age payments start and life expectancy.
  2. Enter the lump-sum offer and your assumed investment return.
  3. Compare lifetime totals and the break-even age.

❓ Frequently asked questions

How are the two totals compared?

Lifetime pension total = monthly pension × 12 × (life expectancy − start age). Lump-sum future value = offer × (1 + return)^years.

How is the break-even age found?

The break-even age is where the growing lump sum catches up with cumulative pension payments — solved by iterating year by year.

Which is better — pension or lump sum?

A pension is guaranteed income for life; a lump sum gives control and inheritance options but carries investment and longevity risk. Weigh both, not just the totals.
